transcript.text: Good morning everyone. I'd like to call this technical and safety huddle to order so we can review the draft run sheet for the feature screening. Before I give my final approval on the venue operating plan, I need both the projection supervisor and the safety and insurance coordinator to walk through the plan with me. Let's start with the key details: the screening is currently placed in Hall A with a capacity of 180 audience members, the Q&A will be recorded for the festival archive, and we're using ordinary two-way audience movement. I'd like to hear from both of you on whether you see any issues with this setup.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a serious issue with the current plan. I checked the distributor portal this morning, and the KDM we have is authorized only for Hall B's secure projector — not Hall A. On top of that, the KDM includes a no-camera-capture condition that applies to both the screening and the Q&A. So as the run sheet currently stands, we can't project the feature in Hall A, and we can't record the Q&A. This portal update came in after the technical run sheet was circulated, so the draft doesn't reflect these constraints yet.

transcript.text: I also need to flag a critical issue. I received the signed fire-marshal certificate after the morning operations meeting, and I haven't attached it to the venue file yet. The certificate caps Hall B at exactly 140 audience members because one exit is under repair. Additionally, the insurer requires a filed crowd-flow plan specifying one-way entry before admission. So if we need to move the screening to Hall B as Leila's KDM issue suggests, we cannot keep the 180 audience capacity from the draft — we'd need to reduce to 140 — and we'd need to switch from ordinary two-way audience movement to a one-way entry crowd-flow plan before anyone can be admitted.
